skill.name: reviewdog
skill.description: Configure reviewdog for automated security and lint feedback in pull requests. The skill provides CI templates, reporter guidance, scanner integrations, and CWE mapping for review workflows.
skill.summary: Route security scanner results into pull request comments with reviewdog.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of prompt injection or malicious data exfiltration in the skill text. Most static alerts are safe documentation examples or expected reviewdog CI configuration. Confirmed risks are the GitLab CI remote installer pipe-to-shell pattern and a predictable temporary Gitleaks report path.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to the shell in assets/gitlab_ci_template.yml.
remediation.suggestion: Download a pinned release artifact, verify checksum or signature, then execute from a controlled path. Avoid mutable branch installers.

remediation.issue: Gitleaks results are written to a predictable /tmp path in assets/pre_commit_config.yaml.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp with restrictive permissions, store reports inside a protected workspace, and delete the file after reviewdog consumes it.

remediation.issue: CI examples rely on platform tokens and several unpinned tool versions.
remediation.suggestion: Document least privilege token scopes and pin reviewdog, scanner, and container versions for reproducible builds.

content.value_statement: Security teams often get scanner output too late or outside code review. This skill helps route reviewdog findings into pull requests with practical CI templates and tuning guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to pipe scanner output into reviewdog reporters.
Provides GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and pre-commit configuration examples.
Covers Bandit, Semgrep, Gitleaks, Hadolint, Checkov, ShellCheck, and custom scanners.
Maps common security findings to CWE and OWASP categories.
Gives tuning guidance for severity thresholds, diff filtering, and failure behavior.
limitations: It provides templates and guidance; it does not run scanners by itself.
Scanner accuracy depends on the configured tools and rule sets.
CI examples need review before use in protected or regulated repositories.
The skill does not replace manual review of complex security findings.

use_cases.title: Add PR Security Feedback
use_cases.description: Add reviewdog comments for Bandit, Semgrep, and secret scans on new pull request changes.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Review Templates
use_cases.description: Create repeatable GitHub Actions or GitLab CI patterns for scanner output and merge gating.

use_cases.title: Tune Developer Signal
use_cases.description: Reduce noisy findings with diff filtering, thresholds, baselines, and tool-specific suppression guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Reviewdog Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up reviewdog for a Python project. Use Bandit and Semgrep. Post comments on new pull request issues only.

prompt_templates.title: Create GitHub Actions Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs reviewdog with Bandit, Semgrep, Gitleaks, Hadolint, and ShellCheck.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Review Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Adjust my reviewdog configuration to block critical findings, comment on warnings, and reduce noise to changed lines.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Platform Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reviewdog rollout for GitHub and GitLab repositories. Include token permissions, scanner selection, and remediation workflow.

output_examples.input: User asks to add reviewdog to a Python repository.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a CI plan with Bandit and Semgrep, token setup notes, failure thresholds, and reporter choices.

output_examples.input: User asks to reduce false positives in PR comments.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests diff filtering, severity thresholds, baselines, and tool-specific suppression locations.

output_examples.input: User asks to map scanner findings to compliance categories.
output_examples.output: The skill maps common scanner results to CWE and OWASP categories and explains how to include references in comments.

best_practices: Pin reviewdog, scanner, and container versions before using generated CI templates.
Grant reviewdog tokens only the permissions required for comments and checks.
Use diff-aware filtering first, then expand coverage after the team handles current findings.
anti_patterns: Do not run remote installer scripts without pinning and checksum verification.
Do not expose full repository tokens to scanners that do not need comment access.
Do not fail every build on low severity findings before tuning thresholds.

faq.question: Does this skill run reviewdog automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates that you review before adding them to CI or local hooks.

faq.question: Which scanners does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common tools such as Bandit, Semgrep, Gitleaks, Hadolint, Checkov, ShellCheck, and custom scanners.

faq.question: Can it support GitHub and GitLab?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include reporter modes and CI examples for GitHub pull requests and GitLab merge requests.

faq.question: How should teams reduce noisy comments?
faq.answer: Use diff-aware filtering, severity thresholds, baselines, and tool-specific suppressions before enforcing hard failures.

faq.question: Does reviewdog need a token?
faq.answer: Remote PR or MR reporters need a platform token. Use the minimum permissions required for comments and checks.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for security review?
faq.answer: No. It improves feedback speed, but teams still need human review for design and complex vulnerabilities.
